comparisons.peer_topic: Human Capital and Leadership Transition Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces intense competition for skilled talent, with demand exceeding supply, and risks from immigration policies and remote work trends. Stock price declines have reduced the value of share-based awards, hindering retention. Additionally, changes in senior leadership, including the retirement of the CEO in December 2024, pose risks of disruption due to the long development cycles and large capital investments inherent in semiconductor manufacturing. Effective hiring, onboarding, and retention of key employees and leadership are critical to mitigating these risks.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address the use of stock-based awards (RSUs) in the context of human capital and retention strategies. AVGO describes the specific structure of its Multi-Year Equity Awards program intended for employees, noting the vesting periods and expense recognition. INTC discusses the strategic use of RSUs and performance-based cash incentives to attract and retain qualified employees, while also noting the risk that stock price declines reduce the retention value of these awards. Both disclosures link equity awards to employee compensation programs, but AVGO details the program's technical parameters while INTC emphasizes the competitive and retention risks associated with these awards.

sentences.text: During the first quarter of fiscal year ended November 3, 2019 ("fiscal year 2019"), our Compensation Committee approved a broad-based program of multi-year equity grants of time- and market-based RSUs (the "Multi-Year Equity Awards") in lieu of our annual employee equity awards historically granted on March 15 of each year.
Each Multi-Year Equity Award vests on the same basis as four annual grants made on March 15 of each year, beginning in fiscal year 2019, with successive four-year vesting periods.
To help attract, retain, and motivate qualified employees, we use share-based awards, such as RSUs, and performance-based cash incentive awards.

Sustained declines in our stock price or lower stock price performance relative to our competitors have reduced the retention value of our share-based awards, which can impact the competitiveness of our compensation.
